profile.address: Friend Plaza, Sarpy Meta Data Center, Papillion, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68059
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 5 of 5 mapped in this cluster, westernmost to easternmost ordering) is part of Meta's Sarpy County campus straddling Papillion and Springfield, Nebraska, southwest of Omaha. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and has expanded it repeatedly since; as of a 2022 expansion announcement the campus plan called for nine buildings and more than 4 million square feet of data center space, up from an initial 1 million square feet, with total investment expected to exceed $1.5 billion, according to the Nebraska Examiner. An earlier 2021 expansion phase alone represented about $400 million of that investment and was expected to double Springfield's city limits. Meta has said the campus draws on 100% renewable wind energy for operations, reflecting the same net-zero, LEED Gold, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments described on Meta's own Sarpy data center fact sheet, which also reports more than $2.5 billion invested, roughly 300 operational jobs once complete, 1,300 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $4.1 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, and a Meta-supported project adding 320 megawatts of new renewable energy generation in Nebraska. Construction has moved more than 3 million cubic yards of dirt and used more than 6,000 tons of steel since 2017, and Meta built a highway overpass to connect sections of the growing complex. By mid-2022, more than 150 full-time employees worked across six operational buildings in Papillion, with employment expected to roughly double as three additional Springfield structures came online; construction supported about 2,000 workers at peak and continued through 2024. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual Sarpy structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

reading.body:
Meta's Sarpy County campus in the Omaha metro area is planned as a nine-building complex across Papillion and Springfield, Nebraska, with more than 4 million square feet total according to a 2022 expansion announcement. Meta does not publish per-building or campus-wide IT capacity in megawatts, exact square footage, or a confirmed final building count, making the true scale of this facility impossible to verify from operator specifications alone. The campus has drawn more than $2.5 billion in cumulative investment since groundbreaking in 2017, with Meta reporting 100% renewable energy operations and commitments to LEED Gold certification and water positivity by 2030.

Sarpy County has emerged as a regional data center cluster alongside Meta, with Google operating eight facilities in the county and Yahoo and Fidelity also present in the area. Nebraska's data center growth has been tied to Omaha Public Power District's renewable generation capacity and state economic-development incentives, though a specific power-purchase agreement naming Meta has not been published. No published megawatt figure exists for any facility in Nebraska in this dataset, leaving the state's total AI-relevant capacity unmeasured.

This building is one of five Meta structures mapped in the Sarpy cluster and represents the only campus-scale commitment Meta has disclosed for Nebraska. Without published power or IT-load figures, the site's contribution to Nebraska's data center capacity cannot be ranked against other operators or placed in national AI infrastructure growth. The campus matters to AI primarily as a demonstration of Meta's willingness to invest multi-billion-dollar capital in renewable-constrained regions, a pattern that signals confidence in wind capacity and local grid development as durable competitive advantages.
